summary.text: 很 is a phonosemantic character: 彳 contributes a semantic cue, while 艮 is proposed as a sound cue because their reconstructed Old Chinese forms are similar, though not identical. Today 很 commonly means “very” or “quite”; its older glosses concern disobedience, difficulty walking, or perversity, and the route to the degree use remains disputed.

formation.text: The character combines semantic 彳 with phonetic 艮. The Shuowen glosses it as “not obeying,” “difficult to walk,” and “perverse”; the relation among these senses and 彳’s precise contribution are unresolved.

components.text: In 很, 彳 is analyzed as the semantic component. Its precise contribution to the early glosses is unclear.
In 很, 艮 is the phonetic component. Zhengzhang’s reconstructed forms are similar but not identical; this sound role does not establish 艮’s oldest graphic referent.

sound_limitation.text: The cited reconstructions support an approximate sound relationship, but do not establish 艮’s original referent or name.

sound.text: In Zhengzhang Shangfang’s Old Chinese reconstruction, the forms are similar but differ in initial, final, and tone. This supports an approximate sound cue; modern Mandarin readings also differ.

history.text: The available graphic record reaches a Shuowen small-seal form for 很. The curated image is a modern seal-script-style rendering of 艮, the proposed sound component, not an early form of the whole character.

uncertainties.text: The relation among the glosses “not obeying,” “difficult to walk,” and “perverse” is unresolved. One dictionary favors “difficult to walk” as the original sense, but this proposed derivation is not demonstrated.

The emergence of the degree adverb is disputed: proposals include grammaticalization from adjectival 很/狠 constructions and Yuan contact involving a degree word written 哏. The date and witness for the proposed Yuan example remain unresolved.

Reported early transmitted-text examples do not establish when their surviving wording entered the texts; some available attestations are indexed search-result transcriptions rather than inspected primary witnesses.

senses.text: The Shuowen glosses 很 as “not obeying.” The accessible transcription comes from an indexed search result, so exact textual details warrant caution.
The Shuowen also gives “difficult to walk.” One dictionary treats this as the original sense and links obstruction to later defiance, but that path is uncertain.

senses.period: Han usage proposed; exact dating unresolved
senses.text: Reference works record adjectival uses meaning fierce or perverse. A scholarly account places this adjective after earlier noncompliance usage, though the chronology remains uncertain.

senses.period: current; emergence proposed for Yuan, exact dating unresolved
senses.text: 很 commonly functions as a degree adverb. Its emergence has been explained either as grammaticalization from adjectival constructions or as a usage associated with Yuan contact and a degree word written 哏; the route is unsettled.

developments.text: A scholarly account proposes a development from noncompliance to a fierce or cruel adjective; this is a proposed sequence, not a verified chronology.

The degree use may have developed through adjectival constructions, or may be associated with a contact-related degree use written 哏. The evidence does not settle whether this was semantic change, grammaticalization, or adoption of a related spoken form with changing spellings.

limitations.text: The early glosses are not securely ordered, and a continuous semantic chain from difficulty or defiance to the modern degree use is not established.
The first degree use’s precise date, reading, and textual witness remain unresolved; the reported Yuan example comes from article notes rather than an independently inspected primary witness.

overview.text: 很 means “very” or “quite” today. It combines semantic 彳 with 艮 as a proposed sound cue: their reconstructed Old Chinese forms are similar, though not identical. Older glosses concern disobedience or difficulty, but their relation to the modern degree use is disputed.

components.text: 彳 marks the semantic side of the character, though its exact contribution to the early meanings is unclear.
艮 is proposed as a sound cue because its reconstructed Old Chinese form resembles 很’s, though the forms are not identical.

takeaway.text: The modern “very; quite” meaning is not a proven direct development from “defiant” or “difficult to walk.”

relationships.text: 彳 is analyzed as the semantic component in 很, though its specific contribution to the early glosses remains unclear.
艮 is analyzed as the phonetic component; the cited Old Chinese reconstructions show an approximate, nonidentical sound relationship.
